judge.reasoning: The system answer perfectly explains and represents the formula for Multi-head attention, explicitly including the Concat operation as requested.

rows.answer:
Multi-head attention is computed by concatenating the outputs of multiple attention heads and then projecting the result using a parameter matrix $W^O$:

$$\text{MultiHead}(Q, K, V) = \text{Concat}(\text{head}_1, ..., \text{head}_h)W^O$$

where each individual head is computed as:

$$\text{head}_i = \text{Attention}(QW_i^Q, KW_i^K, VW_i^V)$$

Here, the projections are parameter matrices $W_i^Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$, $W_i^K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_k}$, $W_i^V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{model}} \times d_v}$, and $W^O \in \mathbb{R}^{h d_v \times d_{\text{model}}}$.

The system answer correctly and comprehensively explains that the late-interaction operator is computed using the maximum dot product between query and document token embeddings, even providing the exact mathematical formulation.

rows.answer:
The late-interaction operator $LI(q, d)$ is computed by taking the sum over all query vectors $\mathbf{E}_q^{(i)}$ of their maximum dot product with each of the $N_d$ document embedding vectors $\mathbf{E}_d^{(j)}$, which is expressed as:

$$LI(q, d) = \sum_{i \in [1, N_q]} \max_{j \in [1, N_d]} \langle \mathbf{E}_q^{(i)} | \mathbf{E}_d^{(j)} \rangle$$
